Team —

We need to lock the infra capacity and unit-econ narrative for the upcoming QBR. Ask is simple: by EOD Wednesday please send the attached playbook template populated with the items below so I can stitch into the QBR deck Monday morning. For the QBR execs want a concise readout (3 slides): 1) current-run rate GPU spend and utilization, 2) forecast & risk case for next quarter, 3) mitigation/operational levers (batching, prefix caching, model-variant fallbacks, reserved vs burst).

Please fill the template with: 
- YTD and MTD GPU spend (dollar) and hours burned, with unit cost per GPU-hour by region
- Current avg/90p token-level latency and per-request batching stats (mean batch size)
- Utilization target and measured (server-side GPU utilization and serving queue depths)
- Quantified impact of batching & prefix/KV caching (token savings, measured latency shift, requests affected)
- Assumptions behind forecast (growth %, new product funnels, reserved capacity commitments)
- Any outstanding holes or asks we should escalate to sales/finance (credits, contract changes)

I attached the playbook template to this thread. If anyone wants to talk through numbers 1:1, block a 20-min slot on my calendar; otherwise reply inline.

Thanks — this will be high visibility.

—Monica

Subject: Re: Infra capacity forecast & scaling playbook — QBR prep

Monica — attaching the capacity forecast, populating the template with the assumptions we discussed in ops sync. Highlights:

- Baseline (run-rate through Aug): $1.32M GPU spend YTD; Aug monthly run-rate $180k. Hours burned (NVIDIA A100-equivalent): ~14,500 Hrs YTD.
- Unit cost: blended $11.75 per GPU-hour (mix of reserved and spot across us-west/us-east).
- Measured serving utilization: average 48% GPU util, 90p at 71% during peak windows (03:00-05:00 UTC traffic spikes).
- Batching: mean batch size is 5.2 for generation endpoints; shifting to aggressive batching (target 7.5) yields ~14% per-token cost reduction but increases median latency by ~28ms for single-user flows.
- Prefix/KV caching: prefix cache reduces decoded token volume by ~18% on the top 20% of requests (large-context retrieval-heavy flows). We have a small regression risk on freshness; measured 2% QoR drop on a sample eval.
- Forecast: base-case +22% consumption next quarter driven by two product launches (search + assistant); risk case +45% if both launches exceed adoption forecasts. We propose incremental reserved capacity purchase phased across the quarter to keep spot exposure below 30%.

Attached: capacity-forecast-v3.xlsx (tabs: assumptions, by-region, unit-econ, sensitivity). I called out the key uncertainties inside the assumptions tab.

-Vivek

Thanks Vivek — good work. A few notes to surface for the QBR story and the playbook: 

- Please add a short table: cost-per-1M-generated-tokens for common model variants (fp16, 4-bit quant) and for typical seq-lens (256/1024/2048). I expect quantization to reduce cost-per-token by ~28% relative to fp16 for batched workloads; we should show both latency and quality deltas.
- Batching/cold-start tradeoff: include expected p99 tail impact and how it maps to SLO breach probability. The execs prefer a % SLO-breach cost mapping rather than raw latency numbers.
- Cache adoption: good that we have 18% savings on top requests. Add the expected operational overhead (cache invalidation windows, two-week rollout).
- Recommend we include a short fallback policy box: when utilization >85% use cheaper model-variant (quantized or smaller) for low-criticality routes; show expected savings and potential quality delta.

I quoted Vivek inline for traceability. Happy to reformat into a single slide.

-Markus
